pages.title: Bilal ibn Rabah
pages.content:
Bilal ibn Rabah was born in Mecca. He was a black slave. His mother and father were slaves, too. His mother was from Ethiopia.

People in Mecca thought Bilal was not important. But Islam made him a free and great man. He was one of the first Muslims in Mecca. He stayed with Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) all his life. He also gave the first Adhan. The Adhan tells people it is time for prayer.

His story teaches us a lesson. The color of your skin does not make you better than other people.

pages.title: Life in Old Mecca
pages.content:
Before Islam, many people in Mecca did not believe in one Allah. They prayed to idols.

Life was not fair. Rich people had a lot of money. They ate from gold plates and drank from beautiful cups. Poor people had very little. Their life was very hard.

Mecca had big slave markets. People bought and sold slaves there. Bilal was one of these slaves. His master was Umayya ibn Khalaf. Umayya was rich and strong. He loved his idols, and he hated Islam.

pages.title: A Hard Life
pages.content:
Umayya was very unkind to Bilal. His family was unkind, too. They called him “the son of the black woman.” This made Bilal very sad.

Bilal worked all day. He looked after the camels in the hot desert. In the evening, he took food to his master. He was always patient.

One day, Bilal heard about a new Prophet, Muhammad (pbuh). The Prophet (pbuh) told people to pray only to Allah. He taught that all people are equal. Bilal thought about this for many days.

pages.title: A Visit at Night
pages.content:
One night, Bilal left his room secretly. It was very dark. He was afraid. He went to the house of Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr was the close friend of the Prophet (pbuh). He was very kind to slaves.

Bilal asked many questions. Abu Bakr told him about Islam: “There is no god but Allah. Allah is One.”

Bilal said, “I want to be a Muslim, too.” Abu Bakr was very happy. Bilal knew his life was going to be hard. But he believed in Allah. He was a Muslim now.

pages.title: “Allah Is One”
pages.content:
Umayya heard the news. He was very angry. He asked Bilal, “Did you leave our gods?” Bilal said, “Yes. Now I believe in Allah.”

Umayya put Bilal in a dark room. He gave him no food or water. He wanted Bilal to pray to the idols again. But Bilal said no.

Then Umayya hurt Bilal very badly. He put a big, hot rock on Bilal’s chest in the sun. He said, “Say good words about our idols, and you can go.” But Bilal only said, “Allah is One, Allah is One.” He was in great pain, but he was very strong.

pages.title: Abu Bakr Helps Bilal
pages.content:
Abu Bakr heard about Bilal. He went to Umayya quickly. He said, “Sell Bilal to me.” Umayya laughed. Then he sold Bilal for some gold. Abu Bakr paid the money.

Abu Bakr took the big rock from Bilal’s chest. He said, “You are free now. You are not a slave.” Bilal was a free Muslim now. He was very happy, and he thanked Allah.

pages.title: The First Adhan
pages.content:
Later, the Muslims went to live in Medina. The Prophet (pbuh) wanted a person for the Adhan. He chose Bilal. Bilal had a beautiful voice. He was also very brave. In Mecca, he said “Allah is One” in great pain.

Bilal stood up and gave the first Adhan: “Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest.” People heard his voice and came to the mosque. Every morning, Bilal gave the Adhan very early. He added these words: “Prayer is better than sleep.” The Prophet (pbuh) was happy with this.

pages.title: Everyone Is Equal
pages.content:
In 632, the Prophet (pbuh) gave his last speech. He taught that all people come from Adam and Eve. Arabs are not better than other people. White people are not better than black people. Only good actions make a person better.

Then the Prophet (pbuh) died. Bilal was very sad. He went to Damascus and died there.

Bilal’s story teaches us a lesson. Skin color is not important. A good heart and good actions are important.

exercises.title: Practise: Was or Were
exercises.question: One or many?
exercises.explanation: One thing: was. Two or more: were.

feedback.incorrect: Life = one thing. Mother and father = two.

exercises.title: Practise: Did Not
exercises.question: Which form is right?
exercises.explanation: After did not, use the verb with no change: did not believe, did not give.

feedback.incorrect: Did not + believe, give.

exercises.title: Practise: Better Than
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: Who is better?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Prayer is better [blank] sleep. Arabs are [blank] better than other people. Only good actions make a person [blank].
exercises.explanation: We use better than for two things.

feedback.incorrect: Find better in Chapters 7 and 8.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Write the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?

errorItems.sentence: Umayya selled Bilal for some gold.

exercises.explanation: “Pay” and “sell” change in the past: paid, sold.

feedback.incorrect: Pay → paid. Sell → sold. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: My Friend
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about a friend.
exercises.question: Who is your friend?
exercises.explanation: Use was born, one past verb and but.

discussionPrompts.question: One “was born in”: “My friend was born in …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend was born in İzmir.

discussionPrompts.question: One “but”: “He is …, but …”
discussionPrompts.example: He is small, but he is very strong.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole story together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: The Adhan
exercises.question: What does the Adhan tell people?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The Adhan tells people it is time for [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “The Adhan tells people it is time for prayer.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Idols
exercises.question: Before Islam, what did many people in Mecca pray to?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “They prayed to idols.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Unkind Words
exercises.question: Umayya’s family called Bilal “the son of the black woman.”
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: They called him “the son of the black woman.” This made Bilal very sad.

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Abu Bakr’s Words
exercises.question: What did Abu Bakr tell Bilal about Islam?
options: “There is no god but Allah. Allah is One.”
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: Abu Bakr told him about Islam: “There is no god but Allah. Allah is One.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4.

exercises.title: Who Is It?
exercises.instructions: Match the name with the sentence.
exercises.question: Who is it?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: Umayya was Bilal’s master. Chapter 6: Abu Bakr made Bilal free. Chapter 7: Bilal gave the first Adhan.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 2, 6 and 7 again.

exercises.title: The Rock
exercises.question: Bilal said good words about the idols.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “But Bilal only said, ‘Allah is One, Allah is One.’”

feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Medina
exercises.question: Where did the Muslims go to live?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “Later, the Muslims went to live in Medina.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentence of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: The Story of Bilal
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Bilal went to the house of Abu Bakr at night.
Umayya put a big rock on Bilal’s chest.

exercises.explanation: Abu Bakr’s house (Chapter 4) → the rock (Chapter 5) → free (Chapter 6) → the first Adhan (Chapter 7).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the story of Bilal.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
